Target audience: University students (computer science/introductory AI)

Section: section_1 — The Problem: Context Blindness

Lecture lines:
Static word embeddings fail to capture polysemous meaning.
Words processed in isolation lose surrounding context.
Imagine a librarian ignoring everything but the first word.

Planned animations:
Fade in title: 'The Problem: Context Blindness' in #FFFFFF.
Display a sentence with scattered, disconnected words.
Highlight specific words to show lack of relationship.
Animate connecting lines between related words.
Final layout showing coherent structural relationships.

Section: section_2 — Core Concept: The 'Spotlight' Analogy

Lecture lines:
Attention provides a dynamic spotlight mechanism.
Highly relevant words cast a brighter glow.
Example: 'it' focuses its light on 'cat'.

Planned animations:
Fade in title: 'Core Concept: The Spotlight Analogy'.
Display a static document text on screen.
Introduce a 'spotlight' beam moving across the text.

Section: section_3 — The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values

Lecture lines:
Query defines what I am looking for.
Key defines what I have to offer.
Value is the core information retrieved.

Planned animations:
Display labels for Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V).
Show Q and K moving to perform a dot-product calculation.
Show output weights applied to V.

Section: section_4 — Mathematical Intuition: Scaled Dot-Product

Lecture lines:
QK transpose measures similarity between words.
Scale by root dk for stability.
Softmax normalizes scores into probabilities.

Planned animations:
Fade in MathTex: 'Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V'.
Highlight QK^T term in #FF00FF to show raw similarity.
Highlight / sqrt(d_k) term in #00FFFF for scaling.
Show softmax function applied to the scaled values.
Final highlighting of the output weighted sum.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis: Multi-Head Attention

Lecture lines:
Single spotlight cannot capture everything.
Multi-Head Attention runs parallel processes.
Different heads capture different linguistic aspects.

Planned animations:
Visualize multiple parallel spotlight beams on text.
Show each head focusing on different patterns.
Combine results into a single enriched representation.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Multi-Head Attention", [
            "Single spotlight cannot capture everything.",
            "Multi-Head Attention runs parallel processes.",
            "Different heads capture different linguistic aspects."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FF7F50", "#87CEFA", "#90EE90"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualize single spotlight on a text
        text_target = Text("The cat sat on the mat.", font_size=30)
        self.place_in_area(text_target, 'B1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        spotlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        spotlight.move_to(text_target.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(text_target), Create(spotlight))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show multiple parallel heads
        heads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5) for color in [RED, BLUE, GREEN]])
        heads.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(heads, 'D1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(spotlight), FadeIn(heads))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Different heads focusing on different patterns
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(start=h.get_top(), end=text_target.get_bottom(), color=h.color, buff=0.1) for h in heads])
        
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        self.wait(2)
